definition: Basic definitions of an electrical circuit and the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance.
core_idea: An electrical circuit is any closed loop containing a voltage source (e.g. generator or battery) and a load; voltage is the potential energy in an electromagnetic field, and current flows from low- to high-voltage areas until equalized (unless continually resupplied by a generator). Ohm's Law (v = iR) relates voltage, current, and resistance/load.
key_points: A circuit is a closed loop of wire containing a voltage source and a load
A load is any device that consumes electricity (e.g. a light bulb)
Voltage (v) is the potential energy in an electromagnetic field; current (i) is the flow of electrons; resistance/load is abbreviated R
Electrons flow from low-voltage to high-voltage areas, equalizing voltage; in a battery this equalization means the battery is dead
A generator continually recreates voltage, so current keeps flowing indefinitely as long as it runs
Current speed depends on voltage and load/resistance; if current flows too fast the wire can overheat and potentially melt
